0.comment: Illuga: Nikita, Starshyna of the Lightkeepers
0.content:
Nikita, the Lightkeepers' Starshyna, is Illuga's adoptive father. He became Starshyna when Sigurd fell, rescued the orphaned boy soon after and trained him himself before housing the orphans with caregivers. He did not want to raise Illuga to die as a soldier, so he kept him in logistics for a year before letting him take the field. Illuga calls him "my old pops" and once "Dad", and borrows his sayings.

Nikita trusts Illuga with the hardest work: the Kipumaki operation and the Lightkeepers' seat in the League. Yet he still quietly asked Flins, and later the Traveler, to keep an eye on him. Illuga says he can hide nothing from Nikita. He worries about Nikita growing older and wants to give him a precious gift for raising him.

Nikita's rule kept the children out of the mead-hall banquets, which were really wakes. Illuga never told him that he would rather be a nightingale than a Winter Icelea.

1.content:
Illuga regularly brings supplies and work papers to Flins's isolated lighthouse, worried that Flins might die alone and unnoticed; Nikita calls him the Lightkeeper closest to Flins. Flins calls him "Young Master" for his polite, roundabout curiosity, offers him endless glasses of water and ends every story on a cliffhanger. Flins helped Nikita decide to let him enlist and later helped steer him toward command.

In the Dottore crisis Illuga learned that Flins believes himself cursed and unable to leave Nod-Krai. He was angry at how lightly Flins took it, asked outright whether Flins was human, got a laugh instead of an answer, and made him promise to come back alive. Afterwards Flins persuaded him to take the League seat. Illuga says Flins neither confirmed nor denied his suspicions, which he counts as an answer.

Flins once lied that his gem came from an auction. After checking, Illuga caught the lie, then confessed that he wanted a gem for Nikita. Flins told him the true story of the Moon Wheel and hinted that the world might give Illuga a gift too. The two also conspire, badly, to skip Aino's classes.

2.content:
Illuga's companion, a nightingale of translucent golden light. It led him out of a mist-made forest during a Wild Hunt illusion and has stayed with him since; he always leaves a place for it by his door. It warns of danger, lights the way, reveals kuuvahki-hidden paths and dispels Wild Hunt fog. In battle it dashes through enemies.

Alia told him that Aedon once belonged to the Torchforger Solovei and was changed into a kuuvahki being in the old struggle against the "Professor". Illuga was unmoved by this. He sees Aedon as one of the ember-carrying nightingales of the Lightkeepers' tale, and hopes to become one himself someday.

Aedon seems to understand speech. It is unflappable even before the Wild Hunt, but it flees into Illuga's lamp at the sound of Linnea's voice.

3.content:
The Lightkeeper investigation squad Illuga leads, formerly under Captain Olsson. It keeps watch over Kipumaki Cliff from Cliffwatch Camp. Members include Anleifr, a gruff ex-treasure hunter who lost his wife in the disaster three years ago; Rollon, whose brother Ivar was carried out by Illuga and can no longer fight; and Bjorn, the squad's studious tactician, who died in 6.3.

Bjorn had missed the old disaster through illness and spent three years preparing; his study of Frostmoon texts found the sealing array's focal points. After his death Illuga ordered the others back and went on alone. When the squad caught up, Anleifr punched him for it, and Illuga declined to punish him. Afterwards Illuga treats the Traveler as a squad member too.

4.content:
Three years before 6.3, an investigation at an ancient ruin on Kipumaki Cliff triggered a Wild Hunt surge. In the night, whispers in a strange mist turned the squad's members against each other. Captain Olsson ordered Illuga to carry the unconscious Ivar to safety and died covering them; only the two survived. The surge spilled beneath the cliffs and killed many civilians before several squads purged it. Nikita sealed the cliff off.

Illuga took command a month later, still asking himself whether he had fled out of cowardice. The Scourge of Endless Decay later used that doubt against him.

5.comment: Illuga: The Scourge of Endless Decay and Bjorn's Death
5.content:
The Abyssal creature at Kipumaki Cliff mocked Illuga for running "three years ago... ten years ago", mortally wounded Bjorn and tormented Illuga with false voices of Olsson, Bjorn and Nikita. Illuga went alone into the Chasm of Endless Decay; the Traveler, Anleifr and Rollon reached him in time, and together they destroyed it and recovered the Spiralblade. The Arrow of Terpikeraunas, fired from Piramida with Illuga's help, then destroyed the Cataclysm Egg at the Pillar of Embla.

At the victory feast Nikita credited the Nightmare Orioles with the most perilous assignment. Illuga said only that he wished Bjorn could be there, and that he would visit the grave to tell him how the city was.

6.content: The legendary previous Starshyna, golden-haired with a violet blade. He led the Lightkeepers south to hold the line in the fighting that saved the child Illuga, and he fell about a decade ago. Investigating Wild Hunt rifts at the Tideseal Stones, Illuga met Sigurd's corrupted, restless remnant, honoured him in a duel, told him that Nikita had rebuilt the order, and promised to visit.

7.content: After Dottore's defeat, Nod-Krai's powers formed a League. Its members included the Frostmoon Scions' Moonchanter, the boss of the Curatorium of Secrets, the Voynich Guild and the Krumkake Craftshop. Flins argued that the Lightkeepers' representative should be upright and caring and should find their worth in group action. Nikita chose Illuga. Nervous, and unfamiliar with Nasha Town's powerful, Illuga accepted because he wants to make Nod-Krai a more welcoming place. At the opening ceremony he wondered whether the Voynich Guild's Tarno had also been pushed onto the stage.

8.content: Illuga first mistook the Traveler for an ordinary adventurer and Paimon for a Jack Frost when he saved them from Abyssal monsters at the Pillar of Embla. Seeing their strength, he brought them into the Kipumaki operation as temporary squad members. The Traveler pulled him back from despair after Bjorn's death. He believes the victory would have cost far more without them, and he now calls them "squadmate", worries about their adventures and cooks for them.

9.comment: Illuga: The Lightkeepers' Oath and the Oath Lantern
9.content: Illuga recites the Lightkeepers' oath with conviction, including its vow to use bones and blood as fuel and make life greater than death. Every Ratnik carries an Oath Lantern, and a Lightkeeper's life is bound to its flame until their mission is done. Finding a fallen predecessor's corrupted lantern, Illuga cleaned it to rekindle and pass on. His own lantern is his old logistics signal lamp.

10.comment: Illuga: Alia, the Silver Lampwick and the Spiralblade
10.content: Nikita sent Illuga to recover the Silver Lampwick, one of the Torchforger's three relics, from the "fae" Alia at the Pillar of Embla. Alia proved to be a human from five centuries ago, trapped in stagnant time, who warned that the "Professor" had returned. When Illuga blamed the Lightkeepers' three-year delay, she told him a dull blade needs honing and called him a child; he protested. The Spiralblade, the relic seized by the Scourge, became the missing arrowhead of the Torchforger's great bow.

11.comment: Illuga: Varka and the Wild Hunt Expedition
11.content: Illuga fought alongside the Knights' Grand Master and calls his fighting skill among the best. During the 6.4 offensive he and Nikita organised the Ratniki's region-wide response. A reconnaissance squad formed at his suggestion was ambushed, and in the final battle he led Lightkeepers from Piramida to Flins's position, carrying Nikita's message that rooting out the Wild Hunt is every Lightkeeper's duty. He hopes the Lightkeepers might one day help people beyond Nod-Krai, as the Knights do.

12.content: Illuga calls Nod-Krai an Elysium built by human hands and generations of Lightkeeper sacrifice. He does not doubt the new goddess, but believes people should rely on their own strength rather than wait for rescue. When Columbina wandered into a restricted area of Piramida, he politely escorted her out.

13.comment: Illuga: Lauma and the Frostmoon Scions
13.content: The Lightkeepers' friendship with the Frostmoon Scions goes back to the Torchforger and the first Moonchanter, who sealed the fiend together. Illuga admires the current Moonchanter's gentleness and learns something on every visit; he suspects she is shouldering more than she shows.

14.content: Before Nefer's arrival the Lightkeepers were constantly at odds with Nasha Town's gangs, which worried Nikita; Illuga credits the Curatorium with making operations much smoother. Nefer teases him as much as Flins does. He leaves messages at the Curatorium when he needs her.

15.content: Aino handles the Lightkeepers' complex machinery and wants them to learn repairs themselves. She was appalled to catch Illuga applying Nikita's rule of hitting broken things. Now he must attend her classes. His escape tricks (a krumkake left in the stove, fish to lure kittens) were all Flins's, and Ineffa had already defeated each of them. Flins then extracted him on "urgent headquarters business".

16.content: A rare fae lady whom Illuga expected to be quiet and graceful. At their first meeting she pounced on Aedon in excitement, and the bird has fled into his lamp at her voice ever since. She thinks Illuga is talented for so young a squad leader, regrets the chaotic first impression and hopes to write an archive entry on Aedon.

17.comment: Illuga: Childhood in Piramida and the mead-hall banquets
17.content: As a boy Illuga helped in the kitchens during banquets in Piramida's great mead hall and learned to cook from the cooks. He noticed that the "uncle" in the records room who gave him lakkaberry pie and the "aunt" who taught him bread had vanished. He realised the banquets were memorials for victories bought with lives. That realisation sent him to enlist. Nikita's later lore places the Arrow of Terpikeraunas inside the same hall.

18.content: Cooking is how he cares for people. In logistics he prepared each comrade's favourite food and granted half-joking requests as surprises. For the Traveler he cooked a troop-sized feast of lakkaberry krumkakes, smoked fish steak, berries and fried meat, and Nightwatch Soup. He says nothing makes him happier than seeing people happy. He dislikes cold food after too many frozen night watches.

19.content: The Lightkeepers compare themselves to the Winter Icelea, the hardy flower that survives Nod-Krai's false springs; Illuga used the image at Bjorn's farewell. A lesser-known tale says the sun is made of countless nightingales carrying burning embers through the night. Illuga privately wants to be such a bird, the light itself rather than the plant. He says the first Starshyna, Solovei, came from the Snezhnayan tundra, lost his home, and found belonging in Piramida; to Illuga, the fortress is a refuge for people like that.

20.content: Illuga and his squad are hooked on the board game "Tabletop Troupe" and are always short of players. Playing with Navia, Jahoda and the Traveler, he kept trying to sacrifice his own character to save the party until Navia told him to stop charging in alone. He admitted he cannot help himself.

21.comment: Illuga: The Nasha Town trade expo
21.content: During the limited-time 6.5 event Where Waves Meet the Reef, Illuga toured Nasha Town's trade expo with Flins, partly to spend time "in the land of the living". He was troubled to see the trader Wislawa selling a fallen hero's musket. She explained that selling it at least fed the living rather than following the dead, and he bought the musket so that Flins could tell him its stories.
